x: Above: 400 metre specialist Ryan Thomas has had a super season. Still a junior, he made his league debut at Birmingham in match two, scored good points in match three and then astounded everyone with a personal record in match four – 47.22.

The 400m saw a welcome introduction to the team for junior Ryan Thomas who ran well for third in the B. With a shortage of one lap specialists the recently injured decathlon champion Louis Evling-Jones held on well in the A race but faded in the home straight and had clearly lost a lot of fitness.

Fabulous pb from Ryan Thomas With William Sharman in Gothenberg, Dom Girdler seamlessly stepped into the A 110 hurdles and despite lack of training due to heavy work commitments finished a good second in the A race.
Ryan Thomas wasn't having anyone in front of him, however; he romped away from the men's 400m field and was stronger than anyone in the home straight.

Jennifer Culley and Ryan Thomas were both solid over 400 metres, with Ryan disappointed not to go under 48 again. The Bill Merryman Cup for the Young Belgravian of the Year goes to Ryan Thomas for his great improvement over 400 metres and his consistent support of our British Athletics League and Golden Jubilee Cup teams.

Four hundred metre star Ryan Thomas was present to receive the Bill Merryman Trophy for the Young Belgravian of the Year. The Tommy Green Cup for the best men’s performance went to Phillips Idowu for his Commonwealth Games triple jump win and the Centenary Cup for women went to 400 metre hurdler Michelle Carey.
